dedupe_keys.name: open source modelica framework for interdependent energy transportation and communication infrastructure in smart and connected communities

description: This record describes an open-source, flexible, integrated modelling framework for designing coupled energy, transportation and communication systems and assessing the impact of their interdependencies, published as an arXiv paper in 2019. The paper argues that infrastructure in smart and connected communities is an aggregate of intertwined public services and that few studies have quantified the interdependency among the three systems during standard operation. It proposes a multi-level, multi-layer, multi-agent approach to model the interconnected systems, and for proof of concept implements preliminary component and system-level models in Modelica, an equation-based object-oriented language. Three case studies of gradually increasing complexity, energy, energy plus transportation, and energy plus transportation plus communication, evaluate the interdependencies, and quantitative analyses show how outcomes deviate as systems are coupled. Coverage is three case studies of a generic connected community. Access: the paper on arXiv, free; the abstract calls the framework open source but the pages read give no repository link or licence. Caveats: preliminary models. It suits interdependent infrastructure design research, and no directly related records are catalogued yet.
